newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs up but top may be in view.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs up but top may be in view.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures crept a little higher again on Tuesday, extending a rally that has pushed yields towards record lows.
But dealers said both markets were still looking "toppish" and may not be able to move much higher.
"For the near term, the market seems to want to go higher, but for the longer term, it is difficult to see how much further it can go," said one Japanese dealer in Singapore.

Dealers said Euroyen and JGBs appeared to be largely ignoring comments by a senior official at Japan's Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) on Monday, suggesting interest rates could rise after the Japanese general election scheduled for October 20.
"At this point the comments come under the category 'rumour'," said one dealer. "But if they are repeated, the effect may be more dramatic."
Both the Euroyen and JGB contracts were pushed down from early highs on Monday after a U.S. news agency reported the LDP official's comments.
Dealers said Euroyen might fall later in the month if the Japanese first-half corporate season was particularly good.
"If earnings move up strongly in the first half, that could be a signal that the recovery is well under way and the era of very low interest rates may be coming to an end," he said.
March Euroyen ended at 99.31 against its IMM close at 99.30. June closed at 99.18 against 99.17.
December JGBs were last traded at 123.17, up 19 from Monday's settle and against an opening level of 123.00.
Eurodollar futures finished mostly slightly weaker on a bout of profit-taking after Monday's strong gains in reaction to a surprise decline in U.S. non-farm payrolls in September.
"It was a retracement...profit-taking," said one Singapore dealer.
The March Eurodollar contract closed at 94.28, down two ticks on the day and against its IMM settlement of 94.28.
